title: Will this shard key spread the peak?
description: Change the routing key, shard count, write rate, and workload skew. The model separates average cluster capacity from the hottest shard and shows the read fan-out paid for extra distribution.

strategies.label: Range by creation time
strategies.detail: Ordered scans are local, but new inserts converge on the active tail range.
strategies.rangeLocality: One shard for a bounded time range
strategies.rebalanceNote: The active range needs proactive splitting; adding idle shards does not move its incoming writes automatically.

strategies.label: Hash by tenant ID
strategies.detail: Tenants distribute well unless one tenant is much larger or busier than the rest.
strategies.rebalanceNote: Moving the hot tenant changes one ownership boundary but can transfer a large working set and its replica copies.

strategies.label: Tenant ID plus 4 write buckets
strategies.detail: A dominant tenant spreads across four owners, while tenant-wide reads must merge four results.
strategies.rangeLocality: Four shards for a tenant-wide read
strategies.rebalanceNote: Buckets can move independently, but the router must preserve the bucket function during dual-read or dual-write migration.

notice: This is an illustrative pressure model, not a database benchmark. Real capacity depends on record size, indexes, transactions, storage engine behavior, replication acknowledgements, and workload burstiness.
